portion_doctrine: Higgsfield OG segments 11-14 are video tutorial transcripts + embedded strategic breakdowns. REAL CONTENT: 5 strategic operator playbooks for AI video production (Popcorn Storyboard Workflow, AI Influencer Assembly, Cinema Director Pipeline, Platform Ecosystem Mastery, 90-Day Sprint to $1M ARR). Rest is verbose tutorial narration, example commentary, and repetitive video showcase demonstrations (80% junk by volume). Boilerplate: UI navigation hints, creator name-drops, generic praise ('cool, isn't it?'), timestamp markers. Gold extracted: named methods, specific numbers (credit costs), exact prompts/workflows, and 5 distinct business playbooks.
operating_rules: Screenshot Trick: Take screenshot of good scene frame and use as Start/End frame reference to enforce position consistency
Audio De-noising: Separate audio from AI video in CapCut to strip unwanted AI-generated sound effects
Constraint Prompting: Use simple prompts; rely on tool Director settings (Budget/Era/Archetype) not manual prompt engineering
Asset Reusability: Create Elements (characters/locations) once, permute infinitely across scenes
Editing vs Generating: Spend 80% time in editor selecting best segments, not chasing perfect AI clip in one shot
Master Image Anchor: Use single high-quality portrait as persistent reference across multi-scene projects
Tagging System: Reference uploaded images via @image[n] syntax in prompts to force AI coherence
Multi-shot Manual Mode: Define shot duration (e.g., 5 sec + 7 sec = 12 sec total) with frame-by-frame control
Character Sheet Locking: Generate character sheets, use as persistent database entry for every scene
Re-run + Re-edit Loop: On failure, either re-run prompt for different output OR edit prompt in LLM to fix specific issue

Fraud-casting: AI interview simulation workflow (static image -> video animator -> speaking prompt -> add ambient audio)
Director's Pipeline: Casting & Asset Definition -> Scene Orchestration -> Voice Consistency -> Post-Production (many-to-few selection)
Multi-shot Prompting: Single prompt creates many different consistent shots while maintaining character location/lighting consistency
90-Day Sprint Model: Day 0-30 discovery+MVP, Day 30-90 iterate to $1M ARR with daily shipping cadence
Click-to-Add Automation: Product URL -> automated ad generation (removes scripting/filming/editing phase for e-commerce)
Storyboard-First Discipline: Never go straight to video; always define frame sequence using Storyboarding tool first
Many-to-Few Selection: Generate multiple takes per shot, select best snippets, use manual post-production to stitch
8-Interview Discovery: Ask 8 industry experts: 'Did you see this result?' / 'How do you achieve this?' / 'What's your core limitation?'
Unified Tagging System: Reference uploaded images as variables when building prompts via @reference syntax

specific_tactics: Use Claude (LLM) to convert simple narrative ideas into detailed, structured prompts maintaining template accuracy
Prompt adjustment workflow: describe issue to LLM -> make explicit in prompt definition -> re-run generation
Model + Seed + Length + Aspect Ratio selection before generation (structured model parameters)
Start frame reference image defines location and character consistency across sequential shots
Multi-reference model: upload character portrait + scene variations to maintain brand mascot across hundreds of videos
Storyboard Auto mode: automatic 4-frame cohesive sequence generation from story prompt + source images
Manual storyboard mode: hand-define each shot duration and sequence (frame-level granularity)
JSON prompt formatting: structure complex sequences as JSON for machine-readable scene definition
Aspect ratio + duration selection: 9:16 (short-form), 16:9 (broadcast), 1:1 (square) with frame-length targeting
Start frame screenshot: take final frame of previous video, use as start frame for next video (seamless scene continuity)
Zoom in/pan camera movements: leave prompt empty, select camera directive (e.g., 'zoom in', 'pan left') for cinematography without complex prompting
Hologram + reference stacking: attach multiple reference images (character + location + object) in single generation
Voice clone reference: use 10-second audio MP3 as custom voice reference, apply across all dialogue scenes
Separate vocal workflow: extract dialogue from source video, export MP3, use as custom voice normalization reference
Attribute detail stacking: specify physical traits (athletic/tall/hazel eyes) + hair (wavy/brown/slick) + outfit (black tuxedo) in single character prompt
Archetype selection: 50+ pre-built archetypes (Lover, Hero, Mentor, etc.) bypass manual personality prompting
Genre + Budget + Era: pre-set project-level constraints (Action/2020s/50M budget) reduce per-prompt configuration
Character sheet generation: automatic output of full character asset sheet (face, outfit, variants) for consistency reference
Quick transformation scenes: morphing/superhero transformation via simple prompt + character switching
Parallel prompt generation: batch 5-10 scene generations per location, select best angles post-hoc
prompts: Give me a detailed prompt to generate a key frame. I want a [simple description]. [Paste into Claude, get expanded detailed prompt back]
Extend sequence with [X] emotion/action. [Used for narrative continuation]
Describe the issue to LLM and make it explicit that this is something we want to define in the prompt [Error recovery]
[Scene description]: Zoom in on [object/character detail] with [camera movement] [For cinematic focus shifts]
Multi-shot: Generate [number] different angles/shots of [action] with [character/object] maintaining consistency [For parallel generation]
Start frame reference: [Character position/location context] -> [Character emotion/action] [For frame-to-frame sequencing]
[JSON formatted shot list]: shot_1_duration: 5 seconds, shot_2_duration: 7 seconds [For manual multi-shot timing]
Friendly, 50-year-old Asian woman, orange yoga outfit [Character detail specification]
Gatsby style mansion lobby, grand twin staircases, glossy marble floor under warm golden lights, elegant yet slightly ominous atmosphere [Location specification with mood]
Male Latino, around 30, athletic, tall, hazel eyes, wavy brown hair, slick back style, mustache [Physical trait stacking]

contradictions: Perfection paradox: Text emphasizes 'do not aim for perfection, aim for variety' but also shows extensive iteration loops when results fail (14:02, 14:33, 15:05)
Automation vs control: Tools promise 'Click-to-Add automation' (removes scripting phase) yet actual workflow shown is highly manual (director settings, prompt engineering, multi-shot curation)
Cost efficiency claim: Positioned as '24-hour commercial for under budget' but actual credits cited (16-192 per scene) with 10+ scenes = significant cost per video
Character consistency: Claims unified tagging guarantees consistency, yet examples show repeated 'morphing', 'skeletal appearance', 'face quality disintegration' issues (14:23, 14:29, 14:39)
Speed vs quality: '90-day $1M ARR' assumes daily shipping + high-value clients, but Higgsfield tool still requires 5-10 iterations per scene for acceptable results
weird_gold: Viral Lego propaganda videos with AI gaining millions of views + political impact (18:48) - suggests AI video already weaponized at scale
Majestic Studios: AI history channel with 189K subs on AI-generated content alone (no personal brand, pure synthetic content)
Interview simulation naming: 'Fraud-casting' is the explicit term for AI talking-head video (honest language, not euphemism)
Journal-level archetype library: 50+ pre-built archetypes (Lover, Hero, Mentor) suggests UI-level personality archetype encoding (Jungian or narrative-design based)
Native audio generation + lip-sync in Seance 2: AI-generated dialogue + realistic mouth movement sync (solves major lip-sync problem at model level, not post-production)
Character sheet as database entry: Output is creature-like database record (face variants, outfit options, physical traits)—suggests persistent identity layer in Higgsfield
JSON prompt formatting for complex sequences: Structured scene definition (shot duration, timing, object rules) treats prompts as machine-readable code, not natural language
Screenshot-as-reference: Workflow allows grabbing ANY frame from PREVIOUS video and forcing it as constraint in NEXT generation (frame-level storyboarding without storyboard tool)
Multi-reference model scaling: Single character asset replicates across 'hundreds of videos without re-training'—suggests template-based character generation, not fine-tuning
Aspiration-to-reality gap: Video shows 'failed attempts' with visible morphing/glitching, yet positioned as broadcast-ready—AI artifacts acknowledged as normal friction, not blocker
gates: Credit expenditure gate: Each scene 0.5-192 credits; monitor per-project budget before attempting multi-scene narratives
Iteration tolerance gate: Accept 30-50% failed generations; budget accordingly for curation phase
Quality gate: Run final outputs through Upscale before publishing (removes AI artifacting per spec)
Character consistency gate: Use character sheet + manual mode upload constraints; verify face/outfit consistency across 2-3 test frames before full animation
Location persistence gate: Use screenshot-as-reference technique when staying in same location; verify floor/wall textures match between shots
Voice consistency gate: Generate 10-second audio reference sample first; test custom voice clone on single short clip before applying to full dialogue sequence
Animation readiness gate: Keyframe must pass visual inspection; no visible morphing/skeletal artifacts before animating (pre-animation audit)
Market entry gate: Conduct 8-10 expert interviews to define one specific technical limitation before building product (prevent premature feature bloat)
